title: Patch: a dungeon fight has a Menu button that asks before it leaves, so Concede is no longer the only way off its board
thread:
**Issue #3932 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #3932: Patch: a dungeon fight has a Menu button that asks before it leaves, so Concede is no longer the only way off its board
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

In a dungeon fight the board has no Menu or Back button, and the app hides its own menus while a board is up. A player who wants to step away mid-fight (to look at their collection, say, or because they opened the game from their phone's home screen, where there is no browser Back button) has only Concede, and conceding a dungeon fight ends the whole run for good. Once this is built, the fight's controls get a Menu button, as a practice game's do. Pressing it mid-fight asks “Leave this fight?” and says the fight waits where it stood. Leaving goes to the Play menu, and the run picks the fight up again when they come back.

## Why

- `apps/web/src/dungeon/fight/FightScreen.tsx:291-329`: the fight's `<Game>` is given `matchStatus`, `heroAside`, `resultActions` and `concedeBody`, and no `controlExtras` or `boardRail`, so no control on the board navigates anywhere.
- `apps/web/src/shell/MenuShell.tsx:160,169`: while a board is shown, the shell drops its nav rail and tab bar (`{board ? null : <ShellNav path={path} />}`).
- Every other table has a way off. Practice passes New game and Menu as `controlExtras` (`apps/web/src/routes/practice.tsx:1064-1087,1120`), each asking first mid-game. The online match (`routes/match.tsx:589-591`), the daily board (`daily/DailyBoard.tsx:219-221`), Duos and the replays draw a `BackLink` in their rail.
- R2972000 built the fight's leave guard (`FightScreen.tsx:189-201`) and its “Leave this fight?” dialog for “every in-app move off it”, but nothing on screen makes such a move: its test reaches the dialog only by calling `navigate(paths.play)` itself (`FightScreen.test.tsx:375`).
- The client installs as a standalone app (`apps/web/public/manifest.webmanifest:7`, display standalone), where iOS draws no Back button at all.

## Proposal

- Pass the fight's `<Game>` a `controlExtras` Menu button, labelled as practice's is (Menu, with Main menu as its accessible name), that calls `navigate(paths.play)`.
- Mid-fight the existing guard holds that move and opens “Leave this fight?”: Keep playing stays, Leave fight goes. Once the fight has its result nothing is held, so Menu goes straight to Play (the result's Continue stays the way on through the run).
- Concede and its run-ending warning are unchanged.
- Add a sentence to R2972000's §11 paragraph, or a ruling in the issue's block, saying the fight's controls carry Menu, as practice's do.

## Where it lands

- `apps/web/src/dungeon/fight/FightScreen.tsx`, `FightScreen.test.tsx`, `dungeon/fight/testids.ts`
- SPEC §15.6 (the fights) and R2972000, through `spec/pending/<issue>.md`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A dungeon fight in progress shows a Menu control; pressing it opens the “Leave this fight?” dialog with Keep playing focused, and the path stays on the fight.
- [ ] Leave fight goes to the Play menu, and starting the run again resumes the same fight where it stood.
- [ ] After the fight has its result, Menu goes to Play without asking.
- [ ] Concede is unchanged.
- [ ] The new tests in `FightScreen.test.tsx` fail without the change, and `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/dungeon/fight/FightScreen.test.tsx` passes.

## Size and risks

Small: one prop on one component, a few tests, a ruling sentence. Difficulty medium. Low risk: the guard, the dialog and the resume already exist and are tested. The only design call is where Menu leads; Play matches the run map's own Back link (`dungeon/map/RunScreen.tsx:123`).
```
